healthy_volatility_detailed_comparison.findings: PARAKH conditions earnings volatility on recovery elasticity and cashflow cushion. For healthy volatile applicants who consistently repay, PARAKH reduces unnecessary risk penalties, lowering the false-positive review rate while awarding higher presentation scores.

distressed_volatility_detailed_compariso.findings: PARAKH preserves robust risk detection for genuinely distressed volatile profiles. When high volatility is coupled with sluggish bounceback, heavy debt, or exhausted liquidity, PARAKH flags defaults with higher recall and precision than the linear baseline.

experimental_design.independent_variable: Information condition (A: Presentation Score Only vs B: Score + TreeSHAP Explanations)
experimental_design.task_prompt: Review applicant telemetry summary, identify top 3 drivers of credit risk, and render an underwriting determination.
primary_hypotheses: H1: Score + Plain-Language SHAP explanations reduce median adjudication time by >= 25% compared to score-only review.
H2: Explanations improve adjudicator agreement on top risk factors by >= 20 percentage points.
experimental_design.target_sample_size: N = 30 credit underwriters, 40 applications per participant (20 per condition)

financial_inclusion_coverage.statutory_interpretation: Across the full synthetic gig worker applicant population (N = 12,000), PARAKH provides an evidence-based credit assessment for 95.06% of applications using non-traditional telemetry (daily earnings, active days, recovery velocity, cashflow buffers).
